title: Directing: board activities and the agile enablement workshop
blurb: Explain the five board activities in directing a project and how the agile enablement workshop keeps agile maturity and agile risks under regular review.
question: Each stage, the project board meets with agile coaches and business representatives to review the latest Agilometer results and plan responses to agile adoption risks. Which workshop is this, and which process does it support?

teach.h: The board directs; the PM manages
teach.body: Directing a project lets the project board stay accountable for the project's success by taking key decisions and keeping overall control, while the project manager handles day-to-day management within tolerances. In PRINCE2 Agile the board pulls information from the project dashboard and the release map rather than waiting for long reports, and steps in through a small number of authorizations plus ongoing direction.

teach.body: Give ongoing direction covers informal guidance at any time: answering requests for advice, escalated issues, exception reports and an updated project dashboard. At the end, authorize project closure compares the original and current PID, approves the end project report, makes sure post-project benefits reviews cover the product in operational use and confirms the updated project canvas. Most benefits are confirmed after closure, although iterative releases can realize some earlier.

To make sure agile maturity and agile risks are assessed regularly, Agilometer assessments are repeated during initiation and every later stage. This happens in the agile enablement workshop, held for the project board, agile coaches and organizational or business representatives. The Agilometer is a risk practice tool: it gauges how well the conditions support agile working, not how a change request should be handled.

teach.caption: Review results, add missing agile adoption risks, rate them, plan practical mitigations.

teach.h: Two workshops that use the Agilometer

rows.label: Also produces
values: Approaches, agile transformation plan if needed

teach.body: Castlegate Insurance's board, led by executive Fiona Grant, authorizes the claims portal project after reviewing the PID and setting project tolerances. At the end of stage 2, agile coach Ravi Patel runs an agile enablement workshop: the Agilometer review shows weak collaboration with the legal team, the group adds a risk about annual leave freezes, rates both, and agrees a weekly legal drop-in. Between stage ends, Fiona gives ongoing direction when project manager Oliver Brandt asks for advice.

teach.text: The agile transformation plan is created in the project initiation workshop (management approaches topic), NOT in the agile enablement workshop. The Agilometer is first assessed by everyone in the project initiation workshop; the agile enablement workshop is where the board and agile coaches review it regularly.

items: Directing: board accountable through key decisions; PM runs day to day.
Five activities: authorize initiation, the project, a stage or exception plan, closure; give ongoing direction.
Stage decisions rest on the project dashboard and updated release map.
Closure: compare PIDs, approve end project report, plan benefits reviews, confirm canvas.
Agile enablement workshop: board, agile coaches, business representatives.
Topics: Agilometer review, risk identification, risk assessment, risk planning.

summary: You can now describe the five directing activities in agile terms and explain how the agile enablement workshop keeps agile maturity and agile risks under regular review. You can also tell it apart from the project initiation workshop.

A.q: In which directing activity does the board approve the project brief and the release map for initiation, and allow the PM to start initiation?
options: Authorize a stage or exception plan
A.why: Authorize initiation approves the project brief and release map for initiation and authorizes the PM to proceed (Table 13.4).

whyNot.0: Authorize the project approves the PID at the end of initiation.
whyNot.1: Ongoing direction is informal guidance at any time.
whyNot.2: That activity approves an updated release map for the next stage or an exception plan.

A.q: Who is the agile enablement workshop held for?
options: Delivery team, product owner and team coach
Project board, agile coaches and business representatives
Project manager, CPO and senior supplier
Users, chief product owner and product owners
A.why: It is a workshop for the project board, agile coaches and organizational or business representatives (13.3.3).

whyNot.0: That group fits team workshops such as team planning and retrospectives.
whyNot.2: That group helps create the project backlog in starting up.
whyNot.3: Users and product owners take part in demos and backlog work, not this board workshop.

A.q: Which topic of the agile enablement workshop reviews earlier Agilometer results and links the risk areas to agile values and transformation objectives?
A.why: The Agilometer assessment review builds a common understanding of key risks to agile adoption (Table 13.5).

whyNot.1: Risk identification adds agile adoption risks not captured in the Agilometer.
whyNot.2: Risk assessment rates probability and impact and prioritizes.
whyNot.3: Risk planning defines practical mitigation steps.

B.q: In which activity does the board review the updated project dashboard and approve the updated release map, or tell the PM to prepare a premature closure?
options: Authorize a stage or exception plan
B.why: Authorize a stage or exception plan uses the updated project dashboard and release map, or can instruct premature closure (Table 13.4).

whyNot.0: Authorize initiation approves the brief and release map for initiation.
whyNot.1: Authorize project closure approves the end project report at the end.
whyNot.3: Ongoing direction is informal advice between decision points.

B.q: What is the main aim of the agile enablement workshop?
options: To assess agile maturity and agile risks regularly
To create the agile transformation plan for the project
To agree team values, norms and delegation levels
To approve the PID and confirm the project tolerances
B.why: Regular Agilometer assessments in the agile enablement workshop make sure agile maturity and agile risks are assessed regularly (13.3.3).

whyNot.1: The agile transformation plan comes from the project initiation workshop's management approaches topic.
whyNot.2: Values, norms and the delegation matrix are project kickoff topics.
whyNot.3: Approving the PID is the 'authorize the project' activity.

B.q: Which topic of the agile enablement workshop brainstorms further threats and opportunities to agile adoption that the Agilometer did not capture?
B.why: Risk identification builds a fuller list of agile adoption risks beyond the Agilometer (Table 13.5).

whyNot.0: The review discusses the Agilometer results themselves.
whyNot.2: Risk assessment rates and prioritizes risks already identified.
whyNot.3: Risk planning defines how to mitigate the prioritized risks.

C.q: Mid-stage, a board member responds to an updated project dashboard with informal advice for the PM. Which process and activity is this?
options: Managing a stage boundary; report stage end
Directing a project; authorize a stage
Directing a project; give ongoing direction
C.why: Give ongoing direction, in directing a project, covers informal advice at any time, including in response to the dashboard (Table 13.4).

whyNot.0: Report highlights is the PM updating the dashboard, not the board's response.
whyNot.1: Report stage end happens at a stage boundary, not mid-stage.
whyNot.2: Authorizing a stage is a formal decision at a stage boundary.

C.q:
Which two statements about directing a project are correct?
1. The agile transformation plan is created in the agile enablement workshop.
2. Agilometer assessments are repeated in initiation and later stages.
3. Authorize project closure makes sure post-project benefits reviews are covered.
4. The board approves the PID when it authorizes initiation.
C.why: Regular Agilometer assessments run in initiation and later stages (13.3.3), and authorize project closure ensures post-project benefits reviews (Table 13.4).

whyNot.0: Statement 1 is wrong: the plan comes from the project initiation workshop.
whyNot.1: Both are wrong: the plan comes from initiation, and the PID is approved in authorize the project.
whyNot.3: Statement 4 is wrong: authorize initiation approves the brief, not the PID.

C.q: In 'authorize project closure', what does the board compare and approve?
options: The original and current PID; the end project report
The project brief; the release map for initiation
The exception report; the exception plan
The team dashboards; the team plans
C.why: The board reviews the original and current PID, approves the end project report and confirms the updated project canvas (Table 13.4).

whyNot.1: The brief and release map for initiation are approved in authorize initiation.
whyNot.2: Exception plans are approved in authorize a stage or exception plan.
whyNot.3: Team dashboards and plans are team-level artifacts the board does not approve.

reteach.title: A school's board of governors
reteach.question: How is a project board like a school's governors?

blocks.body: Governors approve the plan for the year, sign off big changes and answer the head teacher's questions when asked, but they do not teach lessons. Once a term they also check how well the school's new teaching approach is bedding in and what could derail it. That termly check is the agile enablement workshop.

head: Governors
Project board
rows: Termly check on the new approach

blocks.text: Governors do not write the new teaching plan at their termly check; likewise the agile transformation plan comes from the project initiation workshop.

explain.body: Directing a project lets the board be accountable through key decisions and overall control while delegating day-to-day management to the PM.

test.q: Which statement describes the purpose of directing a project?
options: The PM assigns work and keeps the stage within tolerance
The board stays accountable by taking key decisions
The team agrees, delivers and reports on its work
The PM confirms acceptance of the project product
test.why: Directing lets the board be accountable by making key decisions and exercising overall control (13.3.1).

explain.body: At the end of initiation the board approves the PID, confirms project tolerances, commits the people and resources needed, tells the business and authorizes delivery.

test.q: In which activity does the board approve the PID, confirm project tolerances and commit resources?
options: Authorize a stage or exception plan
test.why: Authorize the project covers approving the PID, confirming tolerances and committing resources (Table 13.4).

whyNot.0: Authorize initiation approves the brief before initiation starts.
whyNot.1: That activity approves the next stage's updated release map or an exception plan.

explain.body: Agilometer assessments are repeated in initiation and each later stage, in the agile enablement workshop for the board, agile coaches and business representatives.

test.q: Which workshop holds the regular Agilometer assessments for the project board and agile coaches?
test.why: The agile enablement workshop, in directing a project, holds these regular assessments (13.3.3).

whyNot.0: The project initiation workshop first assesses the Agilometer with the team.
whyNot.1: The progress review assesses stage status and demos the product.
whyNot.3: Release planning sets OKRs and updates the release map.

explain.body: After reviewing the Agilometer and identifying extra risks, the group rates probability and impact, then plans practical steps to mitigate the highest risks.

test.q: Which agile enablement topic makes sure practical steps to implement mitigations are defined?
test.why: Risk planning defines the practical mitigation steps (Table 13.5).

whyNot.1: Risk assessment produces a prioritized list based on probability and impact.
whyNot.2: Risk identification lists extra agile adoption risks.
whyNot.3: The review discusses existing Agilometer results.
